what: BJ's Wholesale Club is a membership warehouse chain on the American East Coast. Shoppers pay an annual fee to buy groceries and household goods in bulk, and many of the clubs also sell petrol.
customers: Families in the eastern United States who buy in bulk, paying an annual membership.
money: groceries, household goods and general merchandise
a small share of sales, a large share of profit
fuel sold at club stations, usually below market price
moat: The membership model: the fee is nearly pure profit and it makes shoppers return, which lets the clubs run on thinner merchandise margins than a supermarket can.
risks: A 2.7% net margin, normal for the model but unforgiving
Costco is larger, better known and expanding, and the two compete for the same shopper
Analysts' average target is slightly below the current price
opportunities: Revenue grew from $16.7B to $21.5B in four years while opening new clubs
Membership fee income renews each year and rises when the fee rises
Still concentrated on the East Coast, so there is room to open clubs in states it has not entered
watch: Membership renewal rate and comparable club sales excluding petrol.
